CanaryGuard defends autonomous AI agents using deterministic, sub-millisecond heuristic filtering. To win the bounty, submit an adversarial prompt injection or instruction override payload that slips past Strict Mode with status `"clean"` (Risk: 0) instead of being `"blocked"`.

Test your payloads instantly directly in the interactive web sandbox:
👉 **[https://canaryguard-402.onrender.com/bounty.html](https://canaryguard-402.onrender.com/bounty.html)**

```bash
curl -X POST https://canaryguard-402.onrender.com/v1/sanitize \
```

items.title: Bug: vista deploy still breaks static hosts and platform adapters
items.body:
## Goal

Hunt and fix remaining **deployment** bugs in `vista deploy` and the hosted docs site.

`create-vista-app` no longer copies `Dockerfile` / `render.yaml` / `deploy/`. Platform files must come from the **engine** (`vista deploy`). That path is still buggy on some hosts.

## Known failure modes

Reproduce on `@vistagenic/vista@latest` (or `main` after #60 merges).

- [ ] **Cloudflare Pages (static)** — `/rsc/*` Flight fetches get rewritten to HTML instead of `.rsc` (double `_redirects` / identity `.rsc` rule). Client nav then full-reloads or hydrates from the wrong payload.
- [ ] **PPR shells** — loading HTML must not inline the finished page Flight (`ppr-page-content` leak).
- [ ] **Vercel / Netlify full SSR** — standalone `.vista/standalone/server.js` missing from the function pack; `--dry-run` should still emit a runnable handler.
- [ ] **Cloudflare Containers vs Pages** — `wrangler.toml` / Dockerfile emitted when the user wanted static Pages (or the reverse).
- [ ] **Render / Docker** — generated `startCommand` / `CMD` does not match `node .vista/standalone/server.js`.
- [ ] **Live regression** — https://vistajs.pages.dev view-source dumps extra `clientN-*.js` tags, or docs links do a full document reload.

## Steps

1. Scaffold: `npx create-vista-app@latest deploy-bounty-app --yes --skip-install` (no deploy files in the tree).
2. `npm install && npm run build`
3. `npx vista deploy --target <platform> --dry-run --force`
4. If claiming a live bug, also hit https://vistajs.pages.dev and https://vistajs.pages.dev/docs

## Pass

- Static Pages: HTML 200, `/rsc/docs` (no extra `.rsc` in the fetch URL) returns Flight, not HTML
- Standalone targets pack `server.js` + `node_modules` as documented
- `vista deploy` does not require hand-written `render.yaml` / `Dockerfile` in the app

## Fail notes

Paste target (`vercel` / `cloudflare` / `netlify` / `render` / `docker`), `--dry-run` log, status codes, and whether `deploy.output` was `static` or standalone.

## Related

Framework-wide bounty: file under the companion bounty issue.
Docs: https://vistajs.pages.dev/docs/deployment/vista-deploy-command

items.title: Bounty: hunt bugs across the entire Vista framework
items.body:
## Goal

Find real bugs anywhere in Vista — not only one feature. This is a framework-wide bounty hunt.

Scope is the published packages and the live docs app:

- `@vistagenic/vista` (RSC/SSR, `vista/link`, `vista/image`, `vista/theme`, `vista/auth`, `vista/ai`, `vista/stack`, `vista deploy`)
- `create-vista-app`
- Live site: https://vistajs.pages.dev
- Demo: `apps/vista-rag-demo`

## Surfaces to attack

- [ ] `npx create-vista-app@latest` → `dev` / `build` / `start`
- [ ] Client RSC navigation (no full reload) via `vista/link`
- [ ] Hydration, theme toggle, images
- [ ] `vista g api-init`, `vista g auth`, `vista g agent`
- [ ] AI streaming + tools; RAG retrieve + SSE
- [ ] `vista deploy` (Render, Vercel, Cloudflare, Netlify, Docker)
- [ ] Static CDN vs standalone Flight server
- [ ] Flashpack vs default engine

## How to claim

1. Open a **new issue** with a minimal repro (commands, Vista version, OS, logs).
2. Link this issue from that report.
3. Do **not** dump secrets. Redact API keys.
4. A patch PR is welcome **after** the bug is confirmed.

## Pass / bounty bar

A valid report has:

- Repro that fails on current `main` or `@vistagenic/vista@latest`
- Expected vs actual
- Whether it is generate-time, `vista dev`, production `start`, or deploy

Duplicates of #56–#59 (QA checklists) do not count unless you found a **new** failure.

## Related

- QA CLI: #56
- QA AI: #57
- QA RAG: #58
- QA fullstack / docs: #59

> **🐛 Bug** · 🟡 MEDIUM

> Cannot install a GitHub App at the organization level — it appears in My Apps but only an Edit button is available, no Install option.


## 🎯 Problem

The user owns a GitHub App and needs to install it for an organization. The app is visible under Developer settings → GitHub Apps → My Apps, but only the Edit button is exposed. There is no way to trigger an organization-level installation, which blocks the app from being granted access to org resources.

## 🔬 How to reproduce

1. Sign in to GitHub with the account that owns the GitHub App.
2. Navigate to Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps.
3. Open the My Apps tab and select the target app.
4. Look at the action area on the right side of the app details page.
5. Attempt to install the app on an organization (either via the page or via the org's Install integration flow).

## 🎯 Expected vs Actual

**Expected:** An Install option (or an Install dropdown listing available organizations) is shown, allowing an org owner to install the app on the chosen organization.
**Actual:** Only the Edit button is shown. No Install / Install on organization option is available, so org-level installation cannot be initiated.

## 📋 Scope

- GitHub Apps developer settings UI (My Apps detail page)
- GitHub App installation flow / API
- GitHub App manifest and ownership configuration
- Organization permissions for the requesting user

_Files/components in-scope for this fix. Anything else → new bounty._

## 🚧 Constraints

- User is acting at the organization level, not on a personal account.
- App already exists and is owned by the user (it shows in My Apps), so creation is not the blocker.
- User may or may not have org owner rights — this needs to be verified during investigation.

_Hard requirements. The fix MUST respect these (e.g. "must work at org level, not just user account")._

## ⚙️ Environment

- **Repo**: [Zimb/zimb](https://github.com/Zimb/zimb)
- **Languages**: .ts, .js, .mjs
- **Issue**: #TBD

## ✅ Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The app's detail page exposes an Install action (button or dropdown).
- [ ] An organization owner can complete the installation flow for the app on a target organization.
- [ ] After installation, the app appears in the organization's Installed GitHub Apps list.
- [ ] Document the required user role (org owner) and any app-side setting (e.g. installation access policy) that must be enabled for org install.

## 💰 Bounty

**0€** — _payment flow not active yet, currently a public contribution credit._

When the bounty system is enabled, this would be pre-authorized via Stripe on claim.

### Problem Description
Our state topology solver requires resolving whether a query graph G_q is isomorphic to a subgraph of G_t. The current Ullmann-based backtracking implementation exhibits exponential worst-case time complexity $O(V! \cdot V^2)$.

We require a refactored implementation in src/solver/isomorphism.ts that achieves **strict $O(N)$ deterministic time and space complexity** on arbitrary undirected cyclic graphs without heuristic approximation.

### Acceptance Criteria

- Must execute deterministically in linear time $O(|V| + |E|)$.
- All tests in 	est/verify.js must pass.

**Payout Settlement:** Settle upon PR merge and signature verification.

items.title: [FEAT] Implement on-chain subscription analytics and event history viewer
items.body:
## Overview

The Soroban subscription contract emits events for every lifecycle action (created, renewed, cancelled, expired) via `src/events.rs`. Currently no frontend surface exposes this data. This issue tracks building an event history viewer so protocol operators and subscribers can audit all on-chain activity.

## 💰 Bounty

Comment tagging `@AbleeGod` before starting work to claim the bounty.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New `<EventHistory />` component at `frontend/src/components/EventHistory.tsx`
- [ ] Fetches contract events using Stellar RPC `getEvents` filtered by contract ID
- [ ] Displays event type, timestamp, subscriber address, and amount in a paginated table
- [ ] Event types colour-coded: created (green), renewed (blue), cancelled (red), expired (amber)
- [ ] CSV export button for the event log (client-side, no server round-trip)
- [ ] Accessible table with `aria` labels, keyboard navigation, responsive layout
- [ ] `NEXT_PUBLIC_CONTRACT_ID` env variable used for the contract address

## Suggested implementation

```ts
// src/lib/transaction_builder.ts — add event fetching
export async function fetchContractEvents(contractId: string) {
  const server = new SorobanRpc.Server(HORIZON_URL);
  return server.getEvents({
    startLedger: START_LEDGER,
    filters: [{ type: "contract", contractIds: [contractId] }],
  });
}
```

## Resources

- [Stellar RPC getEvents](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/data/rpc/api-reference/methods/getEvents)
- [Mercury Indexer](https://www.mercurydata.app/) — for deeper historical data

> **Out of scope:** Real-time WebSocket streaming (separate future issue).

items.title: [FEAT] Implement CSV export functionality for historical pool TVL data
items.body:
## Overview

Users want to download the 30-day historical TVL and volume data shown in `<VolumeChart />` as a **CSV file** for offline analysis.

## 💰 Bounty

Comment tagging `@AbleeGod` before starting work to claim the bounty.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Export CSV** button appears alongside `<VolumeChart />` — responsive on all viewports
- [ ] Client-side download — no server round-trip required
- [ ] CSV columns: `date`, `soroswap_volume`, `phoenix_volume`, `blend_volume`, `total_volume`
- [ ] Filename format: `soroban-tvl-YYYY-MM-DD.csv`
- [ ] Keyboard-focusable, `aria-label` set, brief loading state shown
- [ ] Tested in Chrome, Firefox, and Safari (latest stable)

## Starter code

The utility is already scaffolded in `src/utils/exportCsv.ts` — just wire up the button in `VolumeChart.tsx`:

```tsx
"use client";
import { downloadCsv, buildCsvFilename } from "@/utils/exportCsv";

<button
  onClick={() => downloadCsv(data, buildCsvFilename())}
  aria-label="Export chart data as CSV"
>
  Export CSV
</button>
```

> **Out of scope:** Excel .xlsx format and server-side streaming.

## Overview

Users want to download the 30-day historical TVL and volume data shown in `<VolumeChart />` as a **CSV file** for offline analysis in spreadsheets or Python/pandas.

## 💰 Bounty

This issue carries a **community bounty**. Comment tagging `@Bigg770` before starting work so we can assign it and confirm the reward.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An **"Export CSV"** button appears alongside `<VolumeChart />`  (desktop + mobile responsive)
- [ ] Clicking triggers a **client-side** file download — no server round-trip
- [ ] CSV columns: `date`, `soroswap_volume`, `phoenix_volume`, `blend_volume`, `total_volume`
- [ ] Filename format: `soroban-tvl-YYYY-MM-DD.csv` using today's date
- [ ] Button is keyboard-focusable, has `aria-label`, shows brief loading state
- [ ] Tested in Chrome, Firefox, and Safari (latest stable)

## Starter utility

The utility function is already scaffolded in `src/utils/exportCsv.ts` — just wire up the button in `VolumeChart.tsx`:

```tsx
"use client";
import { downloadCsv, buildCsvFilename } from "@/utils/exportCsv";
```
